svg.title: Attro research roadmap: eight phases and four optional paths
svg.desc: Start by aligning the Pi 0.87.1 recipe with the installed Pi 1.0 release. Improve input and evidence, then choose UI tools, bounded autonomy, or a parallel public-release lane. Compatibility is untested and timelines are estimates. See the companion Markdown report for sources and acceptance criteria.
svg.text: A calmer cockpit. Inspectable outcomes. Bounded autonomy. Reproducible delivery.
13 OCT 2026 · Source + ecosystem research · No installations or product changes
READ DOWN FOR PRIORITIES · SIDE CARDS SHOW ALTERNATIVES, NOT EXTRA REQUIREMENTS
Estimates assume one experienced maintainer. Advance by exit gates; skip branches you do not need.
Reconcile recipe Pi 0.87.1 with installed Pi 1.0.0.
Preserve native MCP, discovery and explicit model choices.
Separate implemented, verified and publicly available.
EXIT: source pins, artifact provenance and capabilities agree.
A · Keep the private daily driver.
Keep queued input and blocking states reachable.
Expose configured shortcuts; preserve draft and caret.
Check short terminals, non-color cues, IME and resize.
EXIT: no lost input; waiting, stopping and errors are clear.
Show changed files, check scope and evidence freshness.
Distinguish pass, fail, stale and not run.
Surface child results without stealing typing focus.
EXIT: every green result has inspectable current evidence.
Do not create a second store.
Separate session rewind, file restore and release rollback.
Test a whole-process isolation workflow before risky runs.
Define budgets, denial, cancellation and unfinished work.
EXIT: recovery drills + failure paths + independent review.
Reuse Chrome DevTools; add Playwright for repeatable flows.
Try Context7 against ten real documentation questions.
Use React guidance only in React / Next projects.
EXIT: named benefit, pinned source, owner and removal path.
No installs made in this audit.
Improve the existing subagent result and lifecycle loop.
One writer per seam; independent tasks only in parallel.
Measure accepted work, total tokens and review burden.
EXIT: better measured throughput without worse recovery.
Clear history, retained-data and redistribution gates.
Prove anonymous pins and clean macOS / Linux install.
Exercise login, nested work, update and recovery.
EXIT: a stranger can run the documented, reviewed product.
Never expose history as a shortcut.
Portable packaging, richer artifact review or local memory.
Team policy or reviewed update PRs only with real demand.
A GUI companion is an option, not the default destination.
EXIT: user problem + baseline + owner + cost ceiling.
Align the baseline → reproduce queue / attention issues → improve shortcuts → pilot review.
Do not spend the first week adding memory, another renderer, or another agent manager.
Public release work can proceed alongside daily UX; phase numbers are not a mandatory serial schedule.
Common foundation: 0 → 1 → 2 UI branch: 2 → 4 Autonomy branch: 2 → 3 → 5
Public release: 0 → 6, parallel with daily UX Horizon: choose 7 only after measured demand
Observed source ≠ rendered defect. Declared package support ≠ Attro compatibility. Historical pass ≠ current pass.
Companion report: 20 UX opportunities · install matrix · competitor patterns · 10 tickets · sources and acceptance gates
RESEARCH ONLY / Runtime UX hypotheses need current-source reproduction. No security or release certification.
